tldr: Morning batch (Sep 4): OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra — live for early orgs with broad ChatGPT/API/AWS rollout in days, the first model rated Critical for cyber and the one behind OpenAI's 'AGI era' declaration (~98.6% ARC-AGI-3); Nvidia confirmed its $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition, with HF staying independent and hardware-neutral. In governance, Sanders and Casar introduced a bill to ban superintelligent AI outright. Open-weight news: MBZUAI's IFM released the six-model K2 Horizon fleet (0.9B→375B, Apache-2.0) and Qwen 3.8 27B hit ~1,500 tokens/s on Cerebras. Tooling: Hermes Desktop gained one-click local model setup, Anthropic previewed deeper Claude Code extensibility and cut safeguard over-intervention ~85%/60%. Altman warned of 'unsustainable silliness' in the compute buildout, OpenAI committed $1B to frontline cyber defenders, and Claude Fable 5.1 cracked a cipher hidden since 1653.

articles.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, declares the 'AGI era'
articles.summary: New flagship live for select orgs, broad ChatGPT/API/AWS rollout in days — first model rated Critical for cyber, ~98.6% ARC-AGI-3, 100K+ GPU training run.

articles.title: Nvidia confirms $12.9B Hugging Face acquisition
articles.summary: Nvidia buys the open-model hub — 18M devs, 3M models; $11.9B to shareholders + $1B retention; HF stays independent and hardware-neutral.

articles.title: MBZUAI's IFM ships K2 Horizon — six fully open models
articles.summary: Most complete open release yet: weights, code, data recipes for a 0.9B→375B fleet, Apache-2.0. MoVA 36B-A4B runs 4B active params at 512K context.

articles.title: Sanders & Casar move to ban artificial superintelligence
articles.summary: Bill would permanently ban superintelligent AI and pause advanced development until a new federal agency sets rules — up to 20 years for individuals.

articles.title: Qwen 3.8 27B on Cerebras hits ~1,500 tokens/s
articles.summary: Qwen 3.8 27B served at ~1,500 tokens/sec on Cerebras — but HN flags flaky tool-calling and a 450K-token/min cap that counts cached reads.

articles.title: Altman warns of 'unsustainable silliness' in compute buildout
articles.summary: Too many neoclouds are announcing massive capacity without customers to back it; falling compute costs could turn billion-dollar projects into bad bets.

articles.title: Hermes Desktop sets up local models in one click
articles.summary: NousResearch: Hermes Desktop auto-detects hardware, picks the best local model, then downloads and configures the runtime — no manual setup.

articles.title: Anthropic previews a much more extensible Claude Code
articles.summary: Early look at deeper Claude Code extensibility — 'a little crazy, and very exciting' — feedback solicited via anthropics/claude-code issue #91870.

articles.title: Anthropic cuts safety over-intervention ~85%
articles.summary: Biology safeguards now stop benign requests 85% less often than at Fable 5 launch; Claude Code sessions see ~60% fewer cyber interventions.

articles.title: Claude Fable 5.1 decodes a royalist message hidden since 1653
articles.summary: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 cracks a centuries-old number puzzle researchers had considered unsolved, hidden in plain sight since 1653.

articles.title: OpenAI commits $1B to protect frontline essential services
articles.summary: Daybreak for Frontline Defenders: $1B to expand frontier cyber AI, training and support for essential services — days after Astra's Critical cyber rating.

articles.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra on ARC-AGI-3 — ARC Prize analysis
articles.summary: ARC Prize's independent take on GPT-6 Astra's 98.6% ARC-AGI-3 score — the eval detail behind OpenAI's headline generalization claims.

articles.title: MoE trick: more active experts per token cuts reasoning tokens 8.5%
articles.summary: New paper: expanding the expert-selection budget at runtime — no retraining — reduced reasoning tokens ~8.5% on Qwen 35B-A4B+ sparse MoE models.

articles.title: sanoTTS: complete TTS in 294k params that runs on a $3 chip
articles.summary: Smallest complete TTS stack: 294k params (337KB) on a $3 microcontroller with 512KB SRAM; the 1.46M variant beats models 3–10x its size.
